text.p: Spain's Telefonica group posted on Friday a 19.8 percent jump in nine-month earnings, fueled by dynamic mobile telephones and international businesses, as well as lower costs.

Telefonica's attributable profit in the nine months rose to 102.23 billion pesetas ($800 million). Revenue from mobile telephony soared 114.8 percent while income from the foreign division rose 15.6 percent to 258.31 billion pesetas.
The figures met market expectations and the shares turned weaker as investors took profits, but dealers were expecting them to rebound.
"These were bang in line with forecasts, maybe slightly better in the sense that (they) are of better quality than I was expecting," said Chris McFadden, telecoms analyst at Merrill Lynch in London.
Operating profit rose to 413.99 billion pesetas in the nine months to end-September on the back of a 13.3 percent improvement in operating income in the same period.

"The results are good. You can see that operating profit has risen, but at a greater rate than in the previous quarter. It's up eight percent at this point versus an increase of 4.5 percent last time round," said Javier Borrachero, telecoms analyst at Central Hispano Bolsa.
He highlighted a 15.4 percent fall in financial expenses after a 2.7 percent decrease in debt and lower interest charges.
"It's one of the best stocks in Spain, with a rising income stream and falling financial costs. It clearly has potential," Borrachero said.
However it was not all good news for Telefonica on Friday.

In a separate statement, the company said its international arm was to challenge a Romanian government decision after the failure of its Romanian unit to win one of two licences to operate digital cellular phone networks there.
The firm said it would start the "appropriate legal action...to ensure that its rights are recognised and protected," it said in a note.
But this minor setback is unlikely to dampen the market's appetite for the shares, which since the beginning of October have risen around 22 percent to Thursday's close at 2,790 pesetas.
It has far outperformed the Ibex-35 index of leading stocks which in the same period has risen around six percent.
Late on Friday, the Spanish government said it would retain special voting rights in Telefonica which ensure it must approve purchases of stakes larger than 10 percent in the group.

Market experts agreed the firm's third-quarter performance should sustain demand for the shares ahead of the public offering of the government's remaining 21 percent stake in the firm, set for early 1997. They said it may gain another 200 pesetas or more before the year-end.

"With the placement coming up we should see it go up a little. I think (the stock) will end the year just under 3,000 pesetas," versus Thursday's close of 2,790 pesetas, one trader said. ($1=126.8 Peseta)
